chapter: Learning music and the early bands
title: Playing for the Jefferson City Buzzards until his last parade in 1920
summary: He played carnival parades for the Jefferson City Buzzards until he took sick; she describes the last parade he played in July before dying in November 1920.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Now for years, Daddy played for the Jefferson City Buzzards. Oh. Many, many years in the carnival tree.

And he played until he died. They still don't know if he did. The Jefferson City Buzzards. And he played for them every time. That's a long day, though. Yeah. And he played for the Jefferson City Buzzards.
Almost up to the time of his death, would you say?
Almost up to the time of his death.

That's right. Well when he took sick, he played that Bulls Parade. And I didn't want him to go play, he was sick. He was 26. He got out of the band when he played the Bulls Parade and come home and got the band. Then the Monday, he had an Artfellas Parade across the river. And I begged him. And this child's godfather played too in the band. And he begged, he said, George, don't go play that Bulls Parade. I'll give you that $10 out of my pocket. He said, no Brown, my word is my bond. And he went and played. I wouldn't get calling to get his breakfast the Monday morning to play that Artfellas Parade across the river. And he said, birthday, why didn't you call me? I said, because I don't want you to go play that parade. And he says to me, I fixed his breakfast, sit down in his breakfast. He says, do you know, you don't want me to go play that parade? He said, but that would be the last parade I'll play. He said, let me go and play that parade. I didn't bother. He come home and got in the bathing up and he said, well, he died. That was in July. And he died in November. And that was the last parade he played. When did he die? 1920. 1920. 1920. November the 14th. 40 years. 40 years. The 14th of next month. Long time ago. Yeah. That's long.
